She is ___ honest woman who never hesitates to speak the truth.
'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (the 'h' is silent), so 'an' is used.
He is ___ university student preparing for competitive examinations.
'University' begins with a consonant sound ('yu'), so 'a' is used despite the vowel letter.
I waited for ___ hour at the station before the train arrived.
'Hour' begins with a vowel sound because the 'h' is silent, so 'an' is used.
___ sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
'The' is used before unique objects such as the sun, the moon and the earth.
___ Ganga is a sacred river for millions of people.
'The' is used before the names of rivers.
He plays ___ guitar very well and performs at local events.
'The' is used before the names of musical instruments when referring to playing them.
She goes to ___ school by bus every day.
No article is used before 'school' when it refers to the institution's purpose of studying.
___ Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.
No article is used before the names of individual mountains or peaks.
He is ___ M.A. in English literature from a central university.
'M.A.' begins with the vowel sound 'em', so 'an' is used.
She is ___ European by birth but has settled in India.
'European' begins with the consonant sound 'yu', so 'a' is used.
___ Netherlands is famous for its canals and windmills.
'The' is used before countries whose names are plural in form, such as the Netherlands.
He migrated to ___ United States in 2010 in search of work.
'The' is used before country names containing 'United', 'States' or 'Kingdom'.
___ India is a land of diverse cultures and languages.
No article is used before the names of most countries, including India.
I bought ___ umbrella from the shop near the station.
'Umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.
___ more you practise, ___ better you become at the skill.
In comparative structures of the type 'the more..., the better...', 'the' is used before both comparatives.
She is ___ best singer in the class.
He is ___ only child of his parents.
'The' is used before 'only' when it means the single one.
___ water in this bottle is dirty and should not be drunk.
'The' is used because the water is specifically identified by 'in this bottle'.
___ water is essential for life on earth.
No article is used when an uncountable noun is referred to in a general sense.
He is ___ doctor in a government hospital.
'A' is used before a singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound.
She is ___ engineer with a private firm in Bengaluru.
'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used.
___ Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of his wife.
'The' is used before the names of famous monuments and buildings.
___ Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on the planet.
'The' is used before the names of oceans and seas.
He is ___ heir to the family business.
'Heir' begins with a vowel sound because the 'h' is silent, so 'an' is used.
___ Himalayas protect India from the cold northern winds.
'The' is used before the names of mountain ranges.
___ Arabian Sea lies to the west of India.
'The' is used before the names of seas.
___ Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world.
No article is normally used before the names of individual lakes.
He is ___ MBA graduate from a reputed institute.
'MBA' begins with the vowel sound 'em', so 'an' is used.
___ apple a day keeps the doctor away.
'Apple' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is used in this proverb.
'The' is used before adjectives to refer to a whole class of people, as in 'the rich' and 'the poor'.
She was elected ___ president of the students' union.
No article is used before a unique official position when it follows 'elect'.
___ English is spoken in many parts of the world.
No article is used before the name of a language used in a general sense.
She has ___ headache and cannot attend the meeting.
'Headache' is a singular countable noun beginning with a consonant sound, so 'a' is used.
He went to ___ bed early after a long and tiring journey.
No article is used in the fixed expression 'go to bed'.
She is (A)/ a honest girl (B)/ who always speaks (C)/ the truth. (D)/ No error (E)
'Honest' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an honest girl' is correct.
He is (A)/ an university student (B)/ preparing for (C)/ the civil services examination. (D)/ No error (E)
'University' begins with a consonant sound, so 'a university student' is correct.
The honesty (A)/ is the best policy (B)/ that one can follow (C)/ in life. (D)/ No error (E)
No article is used before an abstract noun used in a general sense; 'Honesty is the best policy' is correct.
I have (A)/ a good news for you (B)/ about the result (C)/ of the examination. (D)/ No error (E)
'News' is an uncountable noun, so the article 'a' must be removed: 'good news'.
She plays (A)/ the chess every evening (B)/ with her father (C)/ in the park. (D)/ No error (E)
No article is used before the names of games and sports; 'plays chess' is correct.
The gold (A)/ is a precious metal (B)/ used in jewellery (C)/ across the world. (D)/ No error (E)
No article is used before a material noun used in a general sense; 'Gold is a precious metal' is correct.
